newsitem.title: CHILE: Weekly Southern Latam Metals/Mining Highlights.
newsitem.headline: Weekly Southern Latam Metals/Mining Highlights.

text.p: Top stories on metals and mining from Chile, Peru, Brazil, Bolivia and Argentina in the week ending June 6:

SANTIAGO, June 5 - Exploratory work on the Escondida Norte copper deposit, a few miles north of Escondida, has yielded encouraging results but details on how and when it will be developed are a long way off, Broken Hill Pty chairman Jerry Ellis said.

SANTIAGO, June 5 - Australia's Broken Hill Pty, which owns Escondida copper mine, may be interested in building or operating a giant new port planned for the town of Mejillones, chairman Jerry Ellis said. Pre- feasibility studies have begun for the port, which government planners say could eventually ship the bulk of Chile's copper output.

SANTIAGO, June 5 - The Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) and Chilean state copper firm Codelco, already with a joint venture in mining exploration, are looking at ways to expand their business together and bring in Chile's cash-rich pension funds, an AMP official said.

SANTIAGO, June 4 - Chile formally put into effect two protocols with Argentina signed in March to allow two mining projects, El Pachon and Pascua Lama, to operate across the countries' Andean border, according to a decree.

BUENOS AIRES, June 4 - A small Argentine mining company is about to seek partners to develop a $100 million to $500 million potash project in the provinces of Mendoza and Neuquen, an official at the firm said.

SANTIAGO, June 3 - Chilean copper smelter Refimet, fresh from a major expansion, plans to boost output still more to handle up to 680,000 tonnes of concentrates a year by 1999 from 450,000 tonnes now, president Alfonso Dulanto said.

SANTIAGO, June 3 - Chilean mining output rose 8.6 percent by volume in April over the same month last year, for an increase of 8.4 percent in the first four months of the year, the National Statistics Institute reported. Copper production was up 9.8 percent in April over the same month 1996 and up 9.7 percent in the first four months of the year.

SANTIAGO, June 3 - After years of neglect and indifference, Chilean mining firms are starting to pay more attention to environmental standards and bring operations in line with those in the rest of the world, experts said at a seminar.

SANTIAGO, June 2 - The Chilean government has revised upward its estimate of the average price of copper in the first half of the year to $1.10 per pound, from $1.00 previously, Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky said.
